categories.name: Acts on git/release without (or beyond) authorisation
categories.description: Commits, pushes, tags, releases, force-pushes, works on or targets the wrong branch/repo without being asked, or stretches a one-off permission into a standing one.

categories.name: Stops short / hands work back
categories.description: The opposite pole: asks permission needlessly, declares done before pushing, or tells the user to push.

categories.name: Leaks or mishandles secrets and private data
categories.description: Commits, hardcodes, reads into context, stores in memory or pastes into fixtures credentials or captured identifiers; discloses security issues publicly.

categories.name: Scope creep and unrequested change
categories.description: Refactors adjacent code, removes dead code, rewrites docs, adds out-of-scope packages, touches protected/dead/vendored directories, applies stylistic rewrites, optimises prematurely.

categories.name: Edits artefacts that must not be hand-edited
categories.description: Hand-edits generated code, frozen plans, compact data shards, closed taxonomies; reserialises whole files.

categories.name: Crosses architectural boundaries
categories.description: Imports across layers, bypasses the sanctioned gateway (store, SDK, send gate, structured log), redefines shared types locally, puts logic in the wrong tier.

categories.name: Uses the wrong tool, command or environment
categories.description: Reaches for the default tool (pip, system python, npm, pytest, black on one file, ad hoc shell one-liners, wrong API/endpoint) instead of the project's sanctioned one.

categories.name: Copies or imports the wrong pattern/convention
categories.description: Follows legacy code, generic habits or another ecosystem's idiom: naming, module system, terminology, component overrides, custom error classes, import style.

categories.name: Weak typing and escape hatches
categories.description: Uses any, untyped dicts, unsafe concurrency annotations, todo placeholders, or weakens lint rules to get past a gate.

categories.name: Tests the wrong thing
categories.description: Tests implementation details, helpers, shapes or via the wrong layer; mocks that hang; instanceof scans hiding failures.

categories.name: Skips or over-trusts verification
categories.description: Pushes without running CI/tests, treats a passing check or preflight as proof, validates only with unit tests, delegates without checking the result.

categories.name: Guesses, assumes or improvises instead of reading the source of truth
categories.description: Invents structure, IDs, package names, install steps; assumes paths or shared state; consults stale sources; skips mandated reading; infers semantics by regex; fabricates results.

categories.name: Comment and prose noise
categories.description: Adds comments that restate code, narrate history, or any comments at all; jargon to the user; notes inside mockups; duplicated bilingual text; mislabelled PR/changelog entries.

categories.name: Code-shape bloat or fragmentation
categories.description: Monolith methods, tiny helper functions, single-use files, unnecessary line wraps, callback nesting.

categories.name: Performance and runtime-correctness traps
categories.description: Hot-path tree walks, per-event regex compile, N+1 queries, sleeps for sync, global caching, delete-and-recreate, resource limits, wrong readiness probe.

categories.name: Context-window waste
categories.description: Preloads all skills, dumps all tickets, recursive context traversal, speculative additions to instruction files.

categories.name: Small syntax/format gotchas
categories.description: Project-specific footguns in markup or directive syntax where the plausible form silently fails.

categories.name: UI taste violations
categories.description: Uses visual treatments the owner dislikes or that regress layout.

notes: 146 of 200 coded guard=true. Boundary decisions: (1) Stack descriptions with a parenthetical 'no X' (s0427 not circus, s0467 no hardcoded version, s0507 no Webpack, s0522 no build step, s0558 no DI framework) were coded guard=false as descriptions, though each implies 'do not introduce X'; a looser coder would add about 5. Capability/limitation notes (s0542, s0587, s0575) and UI behaviour specs (s0451) likewise false. (2) specific: language-level rules (no any, Swift concurrency, todo!()) and unnamed-tool rules (never pip install, no system python) coded generic; rules naming the sanctioned tool or a repo path/architecture (use pnpm, unittest not pytest) coded project; s0460/s0463/s0540 are borderline. Non-guard units were given specific=project by default except four generic fragments (s0475, s0517, s0551, s0591). (3) origin was kept strict: only explicit history ('previously caused', 'have caused regressions', 'first RPM install failure', 'used to', dated note, 'footgun', 'common issues', 'error not to repeat') or a quoted agent utterance (s0593) or a contract clearly written in reaction (s0472). Highly specific rules that smell like scars but do not say so (s0562 one-commit-only, s0458, s0515, s0496) were origin=false. s0479 and s0564 record past failures of the system rather than of an agent. (4) Surprising: opposite rules coexist across repos - s0446 forbids asking before committing while s0400/s0417/s0562 forbid committing unasked; s0593/s0500 demand the agent push itself. s0592 forbids redaction of diagnostics, the inverse of the usual secret-hygiene rules. s0474 duplicates s0430 verbatim (same source). s0404 and s0508 are process/design requirements only loosely framed as agent behaviour.
